rationale: Start with a broad gradient at moderate temperature to locate the elution window and critical pairs while maximizing the likelihood of observing all 10 compounds. This establishes a baseline for narrowing the solvent window and testing slope and temperature selectivity.

All pairs have substantial resolution margin, so halve the gradient time to reduce the time penalty. Keeping the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed also reveals which critical pairs are sensitive to gradient slope.

The central critical pair is strongly slope-sensitive. A 12-minute gradient tests whether a modest reduction in steepness can recover resolution while keeping the last peak near the zero-time-penalty window.

Raise temperature while holding the gradient fixed to probe selectivity of the unresolved central pair. Faster elution should preserve the zero time penalty, potentially allowing additional gradient shallowing if needed.

The temperature comparison suggests the central pair approaches an elution-order crossover above 40 C, so modest cooling may improve its separation. At 35 C, the other close pairs should retain useful resolution while the last peak remains near the zero-time-penalty window.

Test just below 60 C to separate the new close pair while retaining the temperature-induced separation within the central cluster. This temperature may balance both critical separations without incurring a time penalty.
Injection 6 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the reference method. Test a shorter gradient at the same temperature to see whether that score can be retained with faster elution.

Injection 6 already reaches the maximum score. Test a slightly shallower gradient to increase the slope-sensitive pair’s resolution margin while checking whether the nearly slope-insensitive pair remains above 1.5 and elution stays within the zero-penalty window.

Keep injection 6 as the maximum-score reference and test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to shift selectivity and shorten elution. This probes whether the narrow resolution margins can improve through the solvent window rather than gradient duration alone.

The higher starting organic fraction improved the slope-insensitive pair’s resolution to 1.61. Lengthening this gradient should restore the other critical pair above 1.5 while keeping the last peak within the zero-time-penalty window.

Slightly reduce gradient steepness from injection 12 to lift its remaining critical pair above 1.5 while preserving the improved central-pair separation. This tests the edge of the zero-time-penalty window; the existing CRF 1.000 methods remain the benchmarks.

Return to the established maximum-score region and slightly reduce steepness relative to injection 10. This should increase the solvent-sensitive pair’s resolution while testing how much margin remains for the other critical pair before a time penalty appears.

Refine within the established maximum-score region using a slope between injections 10 and 16. Both neighboring slopes achieved CRF 1.000, so this method should preserve full resolution and zero time penalty while further defining the usable operating window.

Test a new slope between the successful injections 10 and 21, with the endpoint safely above the last peak’s elution fraction. This should retain the maximum CRF while refining the solvent window around the established fully resolved region.
